title: ASHA workers hold indefinite protest in Bengaluru for higher honorarium

tea.why: ASHA workers are protesting over unfulfilled government promises from January 2025 regarding pay revisions and better working conditions.

summary: Thousands of Accredited Social Health Activists launched an indefinite day-and-night protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on November 17, 2026. Organised by the Karnataka Rajya Samyuktha ASHA Karyakarteyara Sangha, affiliated with the AIUTUC, the workers are demanding a fixed monthly honorarium of Rs 15,000, the release of pending incentives, and retirement benefits of Rs 15 lakh, citing years of financial hardship and unfulfilled promises made by the state government in January 2025. Protesters have rejected previous appeals by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Health Minister U.T. Khader to call off the agitation, insisting on a personal visit from the Chief Minister and a written commitment. On November 26, the Chief Minister urged workers to return to their duties, refusing to provide a written assurance and stating that the government would look into their demands during the upcoming legislature session.
organizers: Karnataka Rajya Samyuktha ASHA Karyakarteyara Sangha
All India United Trade Union Centre (AIUTUC)
demands: Fixed monthly honorarium of Rs 15,000
Release of pending incentives and timely payments by the 10th of every month
Rs 15 lakh in retirement benefits
End to compulsory app-based work without adequate devices and support
response: According to sources, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Health Minister U.T. Khader appealed to the workers to withdraw their agitation and resume duties, promising to address their concerns during the upcoming assembly session. However, the Chief Minister rejected the demand for a written assurance, stating that he could not…

crowd.text: The govt’s failure to honour its own commitments has left 40,000 frontline health workers struggling to make ends meet.

updates.text: ASHA workers launched an indefinite day-and-night protest at Freedom Park in Bengaluru, demanding a fixed monthly honorarium of Rs 15,000.
The protest entered its second day, with participants threatening to lay siege to Vidhana Soudha if demands are unmet.
Protesters rejected a video-call appeal from Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, insisting he visit the venue personally.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar told striking workers not to blackmail the government and refused to provide a written assurance.

fr.summary: Des milliers d'activistes de la santé sociale accréditées ont lancé une manifestation indéfinie jour et nuit à Freedom Park à Bengaluru le 17 novembre 2026. de.summary: Tausende akkreditierte soziale Gesundheitsaktivistinnen begannen am 17. November 2026 einen unbefristeten Tag-und-Nacht-Protest im Freedom Park in Bengaluru. Organisiert von der Karnataka Rajya Samyuktha ASHA Karyakarteyara Sangha, die der AIUTUC angeschlossen ist, fordern die Arbeiterinnen ein festes monatliches Honorar von 15.000 Rupien, die Freigabe ausstehender Prämien und Ruhestandsleistungen in Höhe von 15 Lakh Rupien. Sie berufen sich dabei auf jahrelange finanzielle Not und nicht eingehaltene Versprechen der Landesregierung vom Januar 2025. Die Demonstrierenden haben frühere Appelle von Ministerpräsident D.K. Shivakumar und Gesundheitsminister U.T. Khader, die Agitation abzubrechen, abgelehnt und bestehen auf einem persönlichen Besuch des Ministerpräsidenten sowie einer schriftlichen Zusage. Am 26. November forderte der Ministerpräsident die Arbeiterinnen auf, an ihre Arbeitsplätze zurückzukehren, lehnte es ab, eine schriftliche Zusicherung zu geben, und erklärte, die Regierung werde sich während der kommenden Legislaturperiode mit ihren Forderungen befassen.

nl.summary: Duizenden geaccrediteerde sociale gezondheidsactivisten startten op 17 november 2026 een onbepaald dag-en-nachtprotest in Freedom Park in Bengaluru. Georganiseerd door de Karnataka Rajya Samyuktha ASHA Karyakarteyara Sangha, aangesloten bij de AIUTUC, eisen de werkers een vaste maandelijkse vergoeding van 15.000 roepies, de vrijgave van openstaande bonussen en pensioenuitkeringen ter waarde van 15 lakh roepies, onder verwijzing naar jaren van financiële nood en niet-nagekomen beloften die de deelstaatregering in januari 2025 deed.
